overview.text:
**Changed**
- `src/index.ts:parse`: inputs that fail the single-value regex now go to a compound path instead of returning `NaN` immediately [E6, H3].
- The compound path uses a sticky regex `part` (`/iy`). Each part is a number plus a unit, followed by another number or end of string [H3].
- Each matched part is converted by calling `parse` recursively, then added to `total`. Spaces between parts are skipped [H3].
- The compound path returns `NaN` in these cases [H3]:
  - a part does not match [H3];
  - parts have mixed signs (`negative` vs `sign`) [H3];
  - the input has a trailing space [H3];
  - only one part matched (`count > 1`) [H3].
- Added `src/compound.test.ts` with 3 `node:test` cases: sums, rejections (mixed signs, missing or unknown units, junk, commas, tabs, leading/trailing spaces), and single-value plus 100-character-limit checks [E7, H2].
- `README.md`: adds compound examples and the sign rule. It also notes that the `StringValue` type covers single values only, so TypeScript users should call `parse` for compound strings [E7, H1].

**Why**
- The user asked for compound durations summed in ms. Mixed signs and any invalid part must return `NaN`, and single-unit behaviour and the 100-character limit must stay the same [E1].
- The agent left the single-value parser unchanged and reused it for unit conversion, adding a separate full-string compound check [E5, H3].

**Risks**
- Only `src/compound.test.ts` was run: 3 pass, 0 fail [E8]. Existing suites (`parse.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`, `parse-strict.test.ts`, `format.test.ts`) were not run [E3, E8].
- Type checking was not run because `tsc` is not installed [E8, E9].
- The `part` unit list duplicates the unit list in the single-value regex. If one changes without the other, they can drift apart [H3].
- Inputs containing `+` are rejected, and so are tab or comma separators. These are design choices that only the agent's tests cover [H2].
- The 100-character limit is enforced by pre-existing code that the diff does not show. Only the boundary test in H2 covers it [H2].
- The agent grepped `/home/user/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md` (exit 1) and ran `find ..` for `AGENTS.md`, both outside the repo. Neither modified anything [E3, E4].

mechanism.text:
Control flow of the final `parse` in `src/index.ts` [H3]:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["parse(str)"] --> B["existing length check and single-value regex"]
  B -->|"match.groups present"| C["existing single-unit conversion"]
  B -->|"no match"| D["compound loop: offset=0, sign undefined, total=0, count=0"]
  D --> E["sticky regex part.exec at offset"]
  E -->|"null"| N["return NaN"]
  E -->|"component"| F["sign check on component 1"]
  F -->|"differs from first sign"| N
  F -->|"consistent"| G["recursive parse(component 0) added to total; count++"]
  G --> H["offset = lastIndex, skip spaces"]
  H -->|"offset < length"| E
  H -->|"end reached with trailing space"| N
  H -->|"end reached"| I["count > 1 ?"]
  I -->|"yes"| J["return total"]
  I -->|"no"| N
```

- **Entry:** the compound path only runs when the existing single-value regex fails, where `parse` previously returned `NaN`. Single-unit inputs therefore still take the old path [H3].
- **Length check:** the 100-character limit and the empty-input throw sit above the hunk and are not shown in the diff. Tests show a 100-character padded input parses, while a 101-character input and `''` throw [H2, E8].
- **Component regex `part`:**
  - It uses the sticky (`y`) and case-insensitive (`i`) flags, so each match must start exactly at `offset` [H3].
  - Pattern: optional `-`, a number, optional spaces, then a unit from an alternation ordered `milliseconds?|msecs?|ms|months?|mo|minutes?|…` [H3].
  - A lookahead requires the match to be followed by optional spaces plus a digit, `-`, `.digit`, or end of string [H3].
- **Adjacency:** because the lookahead allows zero spaces, `2d3h` splits into `2d` and `3h`. Tabs, commas, `+`, `junk` or a trailing `x` make `exec` return null, giving `NaN` (`1h\t30m`, `1h,30m`, `1h +30m`, `1h 30m junk`, `1h 30x`) [H2, H3].
- **Missing unit / leading space:** `1h 30` fails because `30` has no unit. ` 1h 30m` fails because the sticky match at offset 0 needs a digit, `-` or `.` [H2, H3].
- **Sign check:** `negative` is taken from `component[1].startsWith('-')`. Any later mismatch returns `NaN` (`1h -30m`, `-1h 30m`), while `-1h -30m` sums to `-5_400_000` [H2, H3].
- **Conversion:** each matched component string is passed back into `parse`, so unit conversion stays in the single-value path [H3].
  - `1mo 2ms .5S` tests the alternation order and case-insensitivity, expecting `2_629_800_502` [H2].
  - `1.5h 10s` tests fractions [H2].
- **Trailing space:** the explicit `str.endsWith(' ')` check returns `NaN` [H3]. The lookahead already rejects a trailing space before the end of string, so this branch looks redundant. That is my inference and was not tested in isolation [H3]. Inputs `1h 30m ` and `1s ` both expect `NaN` [H2].
- **`count > 1` guard:** a lone component that reached this path returns `NaN`, so the compound path cannot widen what single values accept [H3].
- **Verification:**
  - `node --test src/compound.test.ts` passed 3/3 [E8].
  - `tsc` was not installed, so there was no type check [E8].
  - The existing suites (`parse.test.ts`, `parse-strict.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`) were not run [E3, E8].
